outcome: Relationships between cesarean, maternal, and neonatal complication rates
Development of a new dyadic maternal-newborn quality measure
Hospital rankings based on different quality metrics
cohort: Nulliparous, term, singleton, vertex deliveries (n=55,841) at 7 hospitals of the Northwell Health system.
finding: The study found significant changes in hospital rankings when using a new dyadic maternal-newborn quality measure compared to traditional cesarean rate-based rankings, highlighting the need for a combined metric.
mod_finding: The new dyadic measure, which prioritizes vaginal delivery with no maternal and no neonatal complications, led to significant changes in hospital rankings compared to rankings based solely on cesarean rates.
